commons.title: Egeribite and Bibite Attires.jpg
commons.description:
The Egeribite and Bibite womanhood celebration is a significant cultural event among the Ibani Ijaw people of Rivers State. It marks the transition of young girls into womanhood and is a rite of passage filled with cultural rituals, dances, and communal festivities. During this celebration, the community gathers to honor and celebrate the maturity of these young women, emphasizing their roles and responsibilities in the society. The event reflects the rich cultural heritage of the Ibani Ijaw people and serves as a symbol of unity it brings families, friends and we'll wishers together during the two days celebrations.
Day one is usually done at her Father's house, it is so because her father was supposed to be the first to inducted her into the womanhood (Egeribite).
Day two takes place at her husband's house which is to fully induct her into the womanhood proper. At this stage she is allowed to tie some set of wrappers as a full grown woman and has passed all the rites.

The unique dance steps and movements during this celebration is special.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption explicitly identifies the Ibani Ijaw womanhood celebration, and the image shows its distinctive ceremonial dress and adornment.

commons.title: Engenni cultural Attire.jpg
commons.description:
A tale of the Engenni people, a story of their great strength and resilience, and how they have overcome the challenges they have faced.
In the beginning, the Engenni people roamed the land, searching for a place to call their own. They traveled far and wide, crossing rivers and mountains, until they finally found a place where they could settle down.
There, they built their homes with loving care, and they worked hard to cultivate the land. They grew crops and raised livestock, and they fished and hunted in the nearby rivers and forests.
But life was not always easy for the Engenni people. They faced many challenges over the years, including droughts, floods, and disease. Yet they did not lose hope, for they knew that their ancestors were watching over them, and that they would guide them through the toughest of times.
And so they persevered, through the good times and the bad, always striving to build a better future for themselves and their communities. They held elaborate ceremonies to honor their ancestors, and they danced and sang to celebrate their culture and traditions.
As the years went by, the Engenni people became known far and wide for their strength and resilience. They were admired by their neighbors, who looked up to them as a shining example of what it meant to be a true warrior.
In honor of the Engenni people, for they are truly a remarkable people, and their story is one of great courage and determination. May their legacy live on for generations to come, and may their spirit continue to inspire us all.

Haah! Ibeh!! Haah! Izon!!
commons.editorial_reason: The caption names the Engenni people and their cultural attire, while the image visibly shows elaborate traditional ceremonial dress.
